title: Linux camera feed fails to decode MJPEG frames
body:
### Tested versions

- reproducible in: 4.6.dev [7ed0b6167618f9c8c5df87c7e83da6003c081368]


### System information

Godot v4.6.dev (7ed0b6167) - Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS 24.04 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - llvmpipe (LLVM 20.1.2, 256 bits) - AMD Ryzen 9 9900X 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 30.19 GiB memory

### Issue description

When using MJPEG format with CameraFeed on Linux, JPEG decoding errors are repeatedly output:

```
E 0:00:22:448   _jpeg_turbo_mem_loader_func: Condition "err" is true. Returning: Ref<Image>()
  <C++ Source>     modules/jpg/image_loader_libjpeg_turbo.cpp:104 @ _jpeg_turbo_mem_loader_func()
E 0:00:22:448   _load_from_buffer: Condition "image.is_null()" is true. Returning: ERR_PARSE_ERROR
  <C++ Source>     core/io/image.cpp:4542 @ _load_from_buffer()
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect a USB camera that supports MJPEG format (tested with Logitech C920)
2. Run the project
3. Select a camera from the Camera dropdown
4. Select MJPEG format from the Format dropdown
5. Observe JPEG decoding error messages in the console

**Note:**
A significant drop in frame rate has also been observed, but it is unclear whether this is due to processing load or frame drops caused by decoding errors.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

https://github.com/shiena/godot-camerafeed-demo
